rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes an Al interlayer beneath a Cr coating, whereas the paper uses a single-layer AlTiCrZrNbTa high-entropy alloy coating with varied Al content; these are fundamentally different interventions.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies PWR primary water (~300 °C) and high-temperature steam up to ~1200 °C, while the paper uses isothermal steam at 1000 °C and 1100 °C; both involve high-temperature steam, but the hypothesis adds a low-temperature water regime and a higher temperature bound not tested in the paper.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes an Al2O3 diffusion barrier formed from an Al interlayer to limit Cr–Zr interdiffusion, whereas the paper's mechanism relies on a composite Al2O3-TiO2-Cr2O3 surface oxide layer from an Al-alloyed coating to suppress oxygen diffusion; the general class of protective oxide formation is shared, but the specific pathway and structural mediator differ.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts reduced Cr–Zr interdiffusion, improved adhesion, and sustained oxidation resistance relative to a Cr coating, while the paper predicts and measures a minimum oxidation rate and oxygen penetration at an intermediate Al content in a high-entropy alloy coating; both predict improved oxidation resistance, but the property direction is general and the specific comparison differs.
